answer: Challenge-delta pricing. Each identity must submit a fresh, verifiably random challenge whose difficulty is set so the marginal batch cost rises with the number of identities active from the same inlet (submission origin). Answers are single-use: a valid response is bound to the challenge nonce and consumed on acceptance, so replaying or copying another agent's answer fails. An attacker cloning N identities pays a rising per-identity compute bill, while honest agents sit on the cheap lower knoll of the curve.
